tripo_part_0.role: robe with hood, stoles/trim, belt, stars

tripo_part_3.role: left sleeve (bell cuff over the left fist)

tripo_part_10.role: staff, carved upper shaft and crystal claw (above the fist)

parts_note: Roles measured 2026-09-29 on the H2 GLBs (part-coloured x-ray renders and shared boundary loops, work/explore). Tris = proposed decimation target per part (collapse), before caps/bridges. td_priority = linear texel-density factor over the uniform world density (face x2, hands x1.75, staff/crystal x1.5, base x0.5).

body.name: SK_Merlin_H2_Body

weld_pairs.why: face opening of the hood (loop 518, z 0.674-0.832); the beard tip on the chest (loop 63, z 0.643-0.661) is a contact, not welded
right armhole (loop 306, z 0.593-0.733); the sleeve lying on the robe side (loop 211, z 0.477-0.573) is a contact, not welded
right wrist: sleeve cuff and fist (loop 205)

body.weld_note: the H2 parts are one surface cut into parts: every seam loop exists on both sides within 2.2e-5 m (measured). Only anatomical seams are welded. The left sleeve (p3) shares ONE loop with the robe (armhole + the whole side contact, z 0.428-0.729) and the left fist (p8) one loop with the robe (contact) and the sleeve (wrist): not welded, so the left arm, the left fist and the robe are separate shells there, each closed by its own cap. Measured 2026-09-29: welding every contact made a skin web between the raised sleeves and the robe in the probe poses arm_l_raise/arm_r_raise
body.cap_note: after the weld the remaining open loops are the contacts that were not welded (left sleeve/left fist/robe, right sleeve side, beard tip) and the contacts with other objects (shoe soles on the base, the fist holes of the staff, the robe hole of the staff contact, a 3-vertex hole on the robe back); each side is closed by a fan so nothing is open when a limb, the staff or the feet move

bridge.why: Tripo modelled no shaft inside the right fist: tripo_part_2 ends in the loop it shares with the fist (source z 0.613-0.648) and tripo_part_10 starts in the loop it shares with the fist (z 0.670-0.680). A bridge between the two decimated loops makes the separate staff whole (seen if the hand is hidden or the staff is posed apart)

base.name: SM_Merlin_H2_Base
base.cap_note: four open loops on the base top where the shoes were cut off (z 0.093-0.098): flat caps, so the base top has no see-through holes

retopo.method_note: per part, largest first: Decimate COLLAPSE (triangulate) on the welded object with the other parts protected (vertex group weight 0, factor protect_factor; the seam vertices shared with the part are decimatable). Measured 2026-09-29 against QuadriFlow (scaled x100 to pass Blender's zero-length-edge check): at equal triangle counts QuadriFlow deviated 5-10x more from the high-poly (sleeves p99 6.5-8.8 mm vs 0.8-0.9 mm; face max 7.9 mm vs 0.8 mm at 3k tris) and needs closed manifold input, so collapse decimation is used; triangle shape is improved afterwards by beautify on near-flat edges
retopo.sharp_note: smooth shading everywhere (the tangent-space normal map carries the relief) except the faceted crystal (sharp at > 35 deg)

uv.note: seams from Smart UV Project per part on a smoothed proxy (islands never cross parts; tiny islands merged), ABF unwrap with a fold fix, average island scale (uniform world density), then island scale x td_priority, one pack of body+staff+base into a single 0..1 atlas; pack margin 5 px of 4096 per island side (measured gap ~2x margin: 20 px at margin 10, 2026-09-29) so the gap stays >= 8 px. Direct Smart UV on the decimated mesh gave 3971 body islands (2184 single triangles), measured 2026-09-29

bake.device_note: CPU for byte determinism: two full GPU (OptiX) runs of 2026-09-29 gave the same meshes/UV/FBX but different texture bytes (53 of 72 output files differed); Cycles CPU with a fixed seed is byte-stable (W4-B bake_ao, re-measured here). Set GPU for speed when bytes do not matter
bake.pairing: per part: low-poly faces of part k (split to a temp object) <- high-poly part k only; all high-poly parts stay in the scene as occluders for AO; low-poly objects are invisible to rays
bake.cage_note: per part extrusion = max(min, factor x measured p99.9 high->low deviation); max ray = factor x extrusion (source metres)

normal.note: geometry only: the 2M-tri high-poly already carries the relief; the Tripo normal maps are 1/4 of the base colour size

ao.note: distance 0.08 x figure height as W4-B atlas.ao_bake; whole high-poly as occluder

maps.downscale: 2x2 box (BC in linear light, normals renormalised)
maps.normal_convention_ue: DirectX (-Y): green of the OpenGL bake inverted; no N_OpenGL file is written (the Blender preview inverts G of N in its shader; a derived copy added 16.5 MB to git)
maps.orm: R = AO, G = roughness, B = metallic (linear)

team_mask.format: L 8-bit linear = cloth (compatible with W4-B M_UM_Figure: lerp by TeamMask.R, TC_Grayscale)
team_mask.rgba_format: R = cloth (same as TeamMask), G = base side band, B = gold trim/embroidery on the cloth parts, A = 255; proposal for wave 4 (TC_Masks/TC_Default)

cloth.note: midnight-blue woven robe, hood and sleeves: blue hue on the cloth parts; the gold trim, the brown belt and the stars fall outside the hue band

base_band.note: side wall of the base (face normal |z| < 0.5)

scale.choice_note: as the previous candidates (profile /2-/4): hood top 45.0 uu above the base bottom, base 24 x 24 x 5 uu (04 §3.4 / 17 AD-CNF-18 working value Ø24; 5 uu = Base_Sidekick). Figure and staff: uniform scale about the source base-top centre, seated on the normalised base top. H2 Tripo base: Ø0.478 x 0.0975 m -> x0.505 gives Ø24.15 x 4.92 uu, so the normalisation is almost uniform

armature.placement_note: measured 2026-09-29 on the H2 high-poly (work/explore/loops.txt, dbg_land): right wrist = centre of the sleeve/fist shared loop (p4|p6, r 0.031); left wrist = centre of the fist/sleeve shared vertices (p8|p3, 155 verts); ankles = centres of the hem/shoe shared loops (p0|p5, p0|p11); toes = front-most low shoe vertex; grip = midpoint of the staff loops entering/leaving the fist (p2|p6 (-0.1606,-0.0147,0.6262), p10|p6 (-0.1589,-0.0143,0.6756)); weapon tail = crystal top vertex; hood top (0.003,0.002,0.888). Shoulders at the top of the armhole loops (p0|p4 z 0.593-0.733, p0|p3 z 0.428-0.729), elbows, hips and knees are inside the sleeves/robe: estimates as in the previous candidate (profile /4), adjusted to the H2 sleeves

groups.why: face and beard: the beard hangs to z 0.62 on the chest and blends into spine

robe to the ankles (rig-contract §9.4): hips with a soft transition to leg_upper only at the hem; the hood (part of the robe in H2) follows head above z 0.70-0.76; armhole rims partly follow the upper arms

seam_sync.note: vertices within radius of a welded seam blend (smoothstep by distance) toward the weights of the nearest seam vertex; seam vertices take the mean of the rules of their parts. Makes both sides of every weld move together (no torn or sheared seam)
